Proposed additions to the repository's PO- series, each earned today:

- PO-7: THE FULL GATE RUNS ON A COMMITTED TREE. Commit, then gate, then push.
  The clean-checkout check cannot distinguish the session's own staged work
  from a leaky suite, and it fails toward red rather than green, so a dirty
  tree turns a one-suite failure into a two-failure verdict.
- PO-8: EVERY WORKTREE-AGENT BRIEF NAMES THE EXPECTED HEAD SHA and tells the
  agent to stop if HEAD is older, and to quote its HEAD back in its report. A
  worktree starts from HEAD, so any prerequisite must be committed before
  dispatch.
- PO-9: ONE SBE SCOPE TASK PER CHANGE, declaring every path the change
  touches, including the progress page. Splitting one change across several
  tasks makes every close fail on its siblings' files.
- PO-10: TO ADD ONE ITEM TO A TRACKED JSON FILE, APPEND THE TEXT. Never
  round-trip through json.load and json.dump; the reserialisation is a
  whole-file rewrite and hides the real change.
- PO-11: A DISPATCH BRIEF'S FILE LIST IS DERIVED FROM THE RUNBOOK, NOT FROM
  MEMORY. Before scoping a release brief, read the step that names how many
  files the change touches. docs/RELEASE.md says a VERSION bump is a
  four-manifest change; the brief that said seven files cost one full builder
  cycle.
- PO-12: STALE SBE SCOPE TASKS ARE CLOSED DELIBERATELY, NOT WORKED AROUND.
  Four were closed today (one with an unreachable base orphaned by the
  2026-08-18 rewrite, three whose bases were 91 commits behind). Each was
  force-closed with its reason recorded and a decision package written; a
  forced close is never read as clean, which is exactly why it is the honest
  instrument here.
